subject: Quality Assurance & Testing
title: HealthCare.gov Launch Failure
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on HealthCare.gov Launch Failure.

hook.text: The US launched HealthCare.gov for millions of users. On day one, only six people could sign up. Six.

buildup.text: The site was supposed to handle 50,000 concurrent users. It crashed under actual load on October 1, 2013.

discovery.text: The system had no end-to-end load testing. Individual components worked in isolation but failed together.

twist.text: 56 contractors built different pieces with no integration testing. Nobody tested the full system until launch day.

climax.text: A rescue team fixed the site in 60 days. The lesson: integration testing and load testing aren't optional.

punchline.text: No load test. No integration test. Six users on day one.

quiz.question: Why did HealthCare.gov fail on launch day?
options: No end-to-end load or integration testing
